abstract_sentences.text: Micro-benchmarking offers a solution to the often prohibitive time and cost of language model development: evaluate on a very small subset of existing benchmarks.

evidence.anchor: Micro-benchmarking offers a solution to the often prohibitive time and cost

abstract_sentences.text: Can these micro-benchmarks, however, rank models as consistently as the full benchmarks they replace?

evidence.anchor: rank models as consistently as the full benchmarks they replace

abstract_sentences.text: And can they rank models more consistently than selecting a random subset of data points?

evidence.anchor: more consistently than selecting a random subset of data points

abstract_sentences.text: In many scenarios, we find that the answer is no.

evidence.anchor: In many scenarios, we find that the answer is no

abstract_sentences.text: We introduce a meta-evaluation measure for micro-benchmarking which investigates how well a micro-benchmark can rank two models as a function of their performance difference on the full benchmark.

evidence.anchor: rank two models as a function of their performance difference

abstract_sentences.text: This approach can determine which model pairs can be ranked correctly by a micro-benchmark, allowing for a finer-grained analysis of the trade-off between micro-benchmark size and reliability.

evidence.anchor: finer-grained analysis of the trade-off between micro-benchmark size and reliability

abstract_sentences.text: Prior work has suggested selecting as few as 10 examples; we find that no micro-benchmarking method can consistently rank model pairs 3.5 points of accuracy apart on MMLU-Pro or 4 points apart on BIG-bench Hard.

evidence.anchor: 3.5 points of accuracy apart on MMLU-Pro or 4 points apart on BIG-bench Hard

abstract_sentences.text: In order to consistently rank model pairs with relatively similar performances, we show that often as many as 250 examples must be selected, at which point random sampling is competitive with existing micro-benchmarking methods.

evidence.anchor: often as many as 250 examples must be selected

abstract_sentences.text: When comparing only 8B instruction-tuned models on MMLU-Pro micro-benchmarks with 25 examples, we find that more than half of pairwise comparisons are not likely to be preserved.

evidence.anchor: 8B instruction-tuned models on MMLU-Pro micro-benchmarks with 25 examples

abstract_sentences.text: Our work provides actionable guidance for both micro-benchmark users and developers in navigating the trade-off between evaluation efficiency and reliability.

evidence.anchor: actionable guidance for both micro-benchmark users and developers
Code and data are at: github.com/dill-lab/micro-benchmarking-reliability

final_judgment.single_storyline: 以 MDAD 将微基准可靠性转成按 full-benchmark accuracy difference 条件化的 pairwise agreement；样本规模、random baseline、同规模模型案例和 fresh-draw 检验都服务于这一主线。[p.4–10]
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: 正文保留问题 gap、Eq. (1)–(5)、四 benchmark、六种方法、source/target 与 50-trial design、Figures 1–6、关键 MDAD 数字和样本规模建议，足以理解指标和主要行动结论。[p.1–10]
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Appendix B/D 给实现、过滤模型、硬件与 runtime；C/E/F/K/L 给操作化敏感性与模型异质性；G–J 给全 benchmark、fresh-draw、whole-subtask 与完整曲线。主文逻辑自足，精确复现与全 setting 比较依赖附录。[p.14–24]
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 1 并置 aggregate correlation 与 fine-grained agreement，Figure 2 将 0.8 crossing 直译成 MDAD，Figure 4/5 用同设置指标和 pairwise-difference 分布补上机制解释。[p.2、p.4、p.8–9]
final_judgment.largest_gap: 没有独立 limitations section；fresh-draw 只覆盖同 task distribution 的 half split，open-ended generation、cross-benchmark shift 和 target-pair distribution 的外推未测。Appendix C/F 只覆盖 threshold/resolution sensitivity。[p.5、p.10、p.15、p.17]
final_judgment.transfer_rule: 效率替代主张应报告 full-set effect size 条件下的 pairwise agreement，在预先声明的 agreement threshold 下给出最低可检测差值，并保留等规模 uniform-random baseline。[p.4–6、p.8–10]
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: 该规则要求模型对、性能指标和任务分布可比较；MDAD 随 target-pair distribution、bucket resolution、agreement threshold 与 task draw 变化，不能在没有新证据时推广到生成质量或跨任务迁移。[p.4–6、p.10、p.15–17]
